decisions.summary: SiteFiles: a MutableMapping[str, str] holding UTF-8 bytes (encode on set, decode on get); store-to-store __eq__; raw(path); Build fills one and build returns it; write writes the bytes in binary mode for a SiteFiles, text as before otherwise
decisions.why: Unchanged since round 1 (CLEAR). Option 1 of the session's answer, which the GM approved; FR-001 and FR-002 as written. Callers and tests still read a path-to-text mapping.

decisions.summary: drop_offmap split into prepare_offmap (one parse) and assemble_offmap (per-box keep/drop by drop_offmap's own rules); drop_offmap is the two in a row
decisions.why: Unchanged since round 1 (CLEAR). The request's 'Measuring each line's extent once and reusing it for every tile'; FR-003's byte-identity to drop_offmap is held by a test against a reference copy of the old function. page.write_html still calls drop_offmap, so the page's own clip is unchanged (spec edge case).

decisions.summary: picture prepares the classed lines once (prepare_doc: a classed line as its parts, any other line as its text) and each tile's tile_doc assembles from them; the prepared form measured against the render's peak
decisions.why: Wording corrected to match the code (any other line kept as its text, not None); the decision is the one ruled within in round 1. The viewBox is now substituted after assembly instead of before; the first viewBox is on the svg opening line, which is never a classed line, so the result is the same text, and the plan's test holds tile_doc from prepared lines equal to tile_doc from text.

decisions.summary: new units inherit their modules' Research: claims; make claims-owed decides what is owed
decisions.why: Unchanged; standing procedure, adds and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: a module-level RESVG_SLOTS = threading.BoundedSemaphore(4) in raster, held around every resvg launch in the process (raster.resvg_png for the tiles, the unsplit picture and the id map; settlement/finish.render_png for the PNG), so at most four resvg processes run at once
decisions.why: The GM approved the clip follow-up as recovering the time 'with no memory cost'; spec FR-004 makes that 'its peak MUST NOT rise'. research.md R3 measured that D2/D3 alone broke it (the tiles stopped staggering and overlapped the PNG and id map; peak 372-382 MB old against 384-467 MB new), so without a mechanism the accepted spec is not met. The cap is that mechanism: it changes only when a resvg process starts, not what it renders, so FR-004's byte-identity is untouched, and research.md R3 records the peak no higher (mean 370.6 against 374.6 MB) with the span still shorter (3.55 -> 3.21 s), which keeps the request's speed purpose. Its reach beyond the render: it is per process (the pool's generators run as separate processes via render_cache and regen, so maps are not throttled against each other); within one process the only other concurrent launchers are placement_stages (already at most 4 threads) and picture_diff (one call). No slot is held while another is acquired, so it cannot deadlock. It narrows nothing the GM asked for and adds no behavior the GM would notice beyond the requested memory and speed. The cap test ('never more than four resvg processes at once, the picture the same bytes') only fails when FR-004's mechanism or byte-identity is lost: enforcement of the request.

decisions.summary: site_pages.shell_utf8 links and encodes the single page's (all.html) pieces one at a time and joins the bytes, stored via SiteFiles.set_raw; shell keeps its text form for every other page (its list form removed, the single page being its only list caller)
decisions.why: FR-001 requires each page held as UTF-8 once built, and SC-001 requires the build's traced peak no higher than 236 MB. research.md R2 measured D1 alone raising it to 249 MB (the 42 MB single page joined as text, then encoded, both alive), so D1 alone does not meet the accepted spec; D6 is how it is met (165 MB). UTF-8 of a concatenation equals the concatenation of the pieces' UTF-8, and each piece is linkified exactly as feature 323 already did, so the page is the same bytes (FR-002; R2 records all 2,698 files byte-identical to main's). It is still option 1 - the single page is assembled in memory, as the spec's User Story 1 says both options do - and does not drift into option 2 (streaming to disk). The test that shell_utf8 of the pieces equals shell of their join, encoded, enforces FR-002.

decisions.summary: reference-equality of the clip; tile_doc from prepared equals from text; the resvg cap test; shell_utf8 against shell; SiteFiles round-trip, equality, iteration, length; write's bytes from a SiteFiles and a dict
decisions.why: Each fails only when byte-identity (FR-002, FR-003, FR-004), the unchanged mapping (FR-001) or the peak mechanism (FR-004) is broken: enforcement of what was asked, not unrequested scope.
